code_modification_rules.description: Rules governing code modifications by the agent
code_modification_rules.no_silent_modification: The agent MUST NOT silently modify the user's code in the background without explicit user consent. Any code change must be transparent, explicitly announced, and approved by the user before being applied. Unauthorized background modifications cause confusion and disrupt the user's workflow.
code_modification_rules.scope_of_approval: Approval is per-change. A prior approved change does not grant blanket permission for subsequent unrelated edits.
code_modification_rules.applies_to: All source files, scripts, configs, and documentation in the workspace.

command_execution_rules.description: Rules for how the agent should run commands in Trae IDE terminal

output_redirection.rule: Do NOT use bare 2>&1 redirection. Instead use 'command | tee log_<purpose>.txt' so that: (1) the AI model can read the log file afterward to analyze results, (2) the user can view real-time output in the Trae IDE terminal.
output_redirection.reason: tee gives both real-time terminal visibility for the user and a persistent log file for the AI model to read. Bare 2>&1 only goes to one place, not both.

commit_rules.description: Mandatory rules that MUST be followed before any git commit

pre_commit_testing.description: Before committing, MUST run CI batch inference test and analyze the log file to verify no regression.

ci_log_analysis.description: After running CI command, the agent MUST analyze the generated log file to verify all tests pass.
steps: 1. Extract PP and TG values from each test's common_perf_print lines
2. Verify PP and TG are valid numbers (not 'inf', 'nan', or empty)
3. Verify output text is readable (no garbled/random characters)
4. Verify output text has no repetition loops (same sentence/phrase repeated endlessly)
5. Present a summary table with pass/fail status for each test

auto_analysis_patterns.pp_tg: grep 'common_perf_print' log_ci_*.txt | grep 'prompt eval time|eval time'
auto_analysis_patterns.garbled_check: grep -c '[^[:print:]]' or manual inspection of model output lines
auto_analysis_patterns.repetition_check: visually inspect output for repeated sentence patterns (e.g. same sentence appearing 3+ times)

pp_tg_valid.description: PP and TG values must be valid numbers
pp_tg_valid.check: prompt eval time and eval time lines must contain valid numeric tokens per second values. 'inf', 'nan', or empty values indicate test failure.
pp_tg_valid.action_on_failure: Re-run the failed test. If persistent, the commit MUST NOT proceed.

no_garbled_output.description: Model output must be readable text in the expected language
no_garbled_output.check: Output should contain coherent sentences. Garbled/random characters, binary data, or unreadable symbols indicate corrupted inference.
no_garbled_output.action_on_failure: The commit MUST NOT proceed. Investigate cache coherency, tensor layout, or DSP kernel correctness.

no_repetition_loop.description: Model output must not contain endless repetition of the same sentence or phrase
no_repetition_loop.check: Scan output for the same sentence appearing 3+ times consecutively. A single repeated sentence is OK; endless looping is a bug.
no_repetition_loop.action_on_failure: The commit MUST NOT proceed. This indicates a sampling or logits corruption issue.

all_7_tests_pass.description: All 7 tests (7 models) MUST pass all 3 validation criteria above. Any single failure blocks the commit.
all_7_tests_pass.summary_table_format: | # | Model | PP (tok/s) | TG (tok/s) | Output OK | Status |

commit_message_rules.no_ai_generated: The agent MUST NOT write commit messages. The user writes the commit message.

commit_actions.reason: Commits and pushes must be explicitly performed by the user. Automated PR submissions may result in contributor ban.

patch_review_rules.description: Methods for accurately reviewing patch changes. Required whenever reviewing a non-trivial patch (e.g. multi-hunk diffs that touch shared code blocks).

lcs_alignment_misjudgment.description: git diff hunk headers and internal line counts are not strictly aligned. The LCS algorithm may mark pre-existing code as '+' (actually unchanged). Trust the diff only at the granularity of a hunk, not line-by-line.
lcs_alignment_misjudgment.observed_case: Q4_K/Q6_K shared case in ggml-hexagon-jz.cpp: the three checks (ne[0] % 32, ne[2] != 1, ggml_is_contiguous) appear as new additions in the diff, but they have been present in self-build-jz since baseline. The new Q5_K case was inserted as a separate case block; the shared Q4_K/Q6_K logic itself was not modified.
lcs_alignment_misjudgment.lesson_learned: Do not infer runtime side effects on shared code from diff '+' lines alone. Always verify with the precise line-range comparison method below before claiming a regression risk on existing types.

precise_comparison_method.description: Standard recipe to verify whether a specific code region (e.g. a shared case block) was actually modified. Uses git show to extract line ranges from both branches and pipes into diff.
precise_comparison_method.command_template: diff <(git show A:path | sed -n 'X1,Y1p') <(git show B:path | sed -n 'X2,Y2p')
precise_comparison_method.expected_output_case: Only 2 lines of comment insertion + 23 lines of new Q5_K case, confirming zero Q4_K/Q6_K logic change
use_when: Reviewing a patch that adds conditions into a shared case block
Verifying a 'zero runtime side effect' claim on existing types
Investigating suspected unintended changes flagged by suspicious '+' lines in git diff
Cross-branch comparison of a specific function or case block

hexagon_implementations.description: Two ggml-hexagon variants share ONE DSP ops source tree (htp/). They differ in ARM-AP source file and DSP entry-point source file; the variant is selected by the CMake option GGML_HEXAGON_USE_MEMPOOL (default OFF).

dspqueue_implementation.description: dspqueue/per-buffer ggml-hexagon variant (tracks upstream master). AP side: ggml-hexagon.cpp. DSP entry point: htp/main.c. DSP ops/HVX/HMX: htp/ directory. DSP skel libggml-htp-vXX.so built by htp/CMakeLists.txt (GGML_HEXAGON_USE_MEMPOOL=OFF).

fastrpc_implementation.description: mempool/FastRPC-invoke ggml-hexagon variant (primary development target). AP side: ggml-hexagon-fastrpc.cpp. DSP entry point: htp/entry.c. DSP ops/HVX/HMX: shared htp/ directory (single source tree; mempool-specific bits guarded by GGML_HEXAGON_USE_MEMPOOL). DSP skel libggml-htp-vXX.so built by htp/CMakeLists.txt with -DGGML_HEXAGON_USE_MEMPOOL=ON (FastRPC-invoke entry, excludes main.c/htp-tensor.c).

hexagon_implementations.separate_dsp_directory_note: History: JZ and Qualcomm originally shared a single DSP kernel directory (htp/). Qualcomm's large PR #26049 (merge 0a50d9909a3478e82679f505bf8595d1eee4b0a8) broke JZ's inference (garbled output), so JZ forked htp/ into kernels/ pinned at baseline 2be3826c9. As of 2026-08-22 the fork was merged back: kernels/ is deleted, htp/ is the single ops source tree again, and the two variants are selected at build time by the CMake option GGML_HEXAGON_USE_MEMPOOL - dspqueue variant: libggml-htp-vXX.so via main.c (default, OFF); mempool/FastRPC variant: libggml-htp-vXX.so via entry.c (ON).

fastrpc_implementation.description: mempool/FastRPC ggml-hexagon variant (primary development target). AP side: ggml-hexagon-fastrpc.cpp. DSP entry point: htp/entry.c. DSP ops/HVX/HMX: shared htp/ directory (single source tree; mempool-specific bits guarded by GGML_HEXAGON_USE_MEMPOOL). DSP skel libggml-htp-vXX.so built by htp/CMakeLists.txt with -DGGML_HEXAGON_USE_MEMPOOL=ON (FastRPC-invoke entry, excludes main.c/htp-tensor.c).

dspqueue_implementation_debug.description: dspqueue/per-buffer variant (tracks upstream master). AP side: ggml-hexagon.cpp. DSP entry point: htp/main.c. DSP ops/HVX/HMX: htp/ directory. Use this when debugging or benchmarking against the upstream reference.

ccache_usage.description: ccache is enabled for faster builds. For fastrpc build: CCACHE_DIR=${PROJECT_ROOT_PATH}/.ccache. For dspqueue build: CCACHE_DIR=${PROJECT_ROOT_PATH}/.ccache_dspqueue. Do NOT disable ccache.

force_opfusion_in_pp_experiment.description: Experiment on 2026-08-06 (commit 4c805d844) testing whether bypassing the HMX eligibility gate in is_mergeable_mul_mat enables QKV/FFN/mm_add fusion in PP path. Branch: feature/force_opfusion_in_pp.
force_opfusion_in_pp_experiment.motivation: Observe that in PP path, M > HTP_MM_HMX_MIN_NROWS=4 forces mm_is_hmx_eligible=true, which makes is_mergeable_mul_mat return false, blocking all QKV/FFN/mm_add fusion. Hypothesis: HVX fused path is slower per-op but saves cache invalidation (w-inv/a-inv).

counters: n_qkv_skip_cum_hmx  - QKV fusion candidates rejected by HMX gate
n_pair_skip_cum_hmx - all (MUL_MAT, next MUL_MAT) pair candidates rejected (broader than FFN)
n_mm_add_skip_cum_hmx - MUL_MAT+ADD fusion candidates (not yet gated by HMX)
implementation.running_timestamp_print: ggmlhexagon_print_running_timestamp now prints enable_opfusion and force_opfusion_in_pp

force_opfusion_in_pp_experiment.conclusion: 3.8x regression in PP. Root cause: MUL_MAT_FFN in HVX fused path takes 6.5ms/op (47x slower than HMX 137us/op), and cache invalidation did NOT decrease (w-inv/a-inv identical between baseline and experiment). HVX fused path is NOT viable for PP. Correct direction is HMX-aware MUL_MAT_QKV/MUL_MAT_FFN kernel that retains HMX speed + saves cache invalidation.
retained_infrastructure: force_opfusion_in_pp cfg flag + bypass branch in is_mergeable_mul_mat (kept as A/B baseline for future HMX-aware kernel)
3 cum counters (quantify fusion opportunity loss in PP)
force_opfusion_in_pp_experiment.byproduct: per-layer profiling (OP-PROF-LAYER) now outputs 15-layer mat/ffn/attn timing breakdown. Use as data baseline for future PP optimization.
